summary: Caution Advisory for blue-green algae at the WEST swim beach.
detail: Blue-green algae advisories move between caution and danger week to week and clear faster than a month, so this is among the shortest-lived facts in this project. Ordinance 38 s.801.1 already bars every animal from bathing beaches, leashed or not, so a dog or cat is not affected by the advisory -- it was never allowed there.

summary: Caution Advisory for blue-green algae at the EAST swim beach.
detail: Posted separately from the west beach; the two are advised independently.

summary: Golden mussels detected at Contra Loma: a boat launched there is quarantined for 30 days from Del Valle and other inspected lakes.
detail: Clean, drain and dry any vessel before launching anywhere. Boat bands are honoured only at the lake that issued them. Recorded against Del Valle rather than Contra Loma because Del Valle is the park this project holds; the detection itself is at Contra Loma, which is also where Star Mine Group Camp parties park, and neither Contra Loma nor Lake Chabot has a row here for their own advisories to attach to.

summary: Dry Creek Garden is closed until further notice, for storm damage.
location: Dry Creek Garden, end of May Road, Union City
detail: Posted on the park page as 'Due to storm damage Dry Creek Garden is closed until further notice.' The garden's published hours are Thursday to Saturday 10am-4pm, so the hours and the closure sit on the same page and only the closure is current. Rated INFO rather than caution because it shuts an attraction, not a route or a camp: nothing about Arroyo Flats depends on it. It does close one of the park's two disabled-parking areas, the Dry Creek Garden lot at the end of May Road in Union City -- whether that lot is closed with the garden is not stated. The fourth storm-damage closure in this table, after two at Anthony Chabot, one at Briones and one at Round Valley. THE GARDEN IS ACTUALLY IN THE ADJOINING PARK, which this row did not know when it was written. Dry Creek Pioneer's address is 550 May Road, Union City, the garden sits at the end of May Road, and the shared map puts MEYERS DRY CREEK GARDEN in the Dry Creek Pioneer half. IT STAYS SCOPED TO GARIN, deliberately, and a second row scoped to Dry Creek Pioneer was written and then deleted: nothing in this dataset sits in Dry Creek Pioneer, so an advisory scoped there can never reach a plan, and EBRPD posts this closure on Garin's page anyway. A row nobody can be shown is filing-cabinet work. What would fix the scope properly is a unit that can name a paired parkland -- two parks with one map, one phone extension and one combined acreage. DRY CREEK PIONEER'S OWN PAGE IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN GARIN'S: 'The garden is currently closed due to storm damage. An estimated reopening is not yet determined.' No estimate is a stronger statement than 'until further notice' -- it says EBRPD has been asked and does not know. This advisory will therefore never expire on its own; it will go stale and report its age. THE ADJACENT IRIS GARDEN IS NOT CLOSED: open seasonally in spring, usually two months, Thursdays to Sundays 10am-4pm, and the map marks it 'Open in spring'. The main garden's suspended hours are Thursday to Saturday 10am-4pm.

summary: Stream Trail is closed for repairs from Trail's End through Fern Trail.
location: Stream Trail, Trail's End through Fern Trail
detail: 'Sections of the Stream Trail ... will be closed for repairs beginning Mon., Aug. 24, 2026 from Trail's End through Fern Trail.' THE FIRST ADVISORY HERE WITH A START DATE. Every other row in this table was already in force when it was read, so `starts` has never carried a value; this one began three weeks before it was read and the field finally earns its place. NO END IS PUBLISHED, so it is filed open-ended and will report its age rather than expiring. WHAT IT SHUTS: Stream Trail is the park's valley-floor spine, and the map puts Trail's End, Big Bend Meadow, Orchard, Old Church and Fern Dell along it -- named places some of which are reservable picnic sites and some of which may be the 'several' group camps the park page claims. Until those are told apart, whether this closure reaches a camp is unknown, which is a reason to find out rather than a reason to rate it lower. The children's play structure a quarter mile down Stream Trail from Canyon Meadow is on this trail too. EBRPD dates the notice 'Updated September 16, 2026', the day it was read.

summary: A second Stream Trail shutdown at Old Church picnic site, late September into early October.
location: Stream Trail at Old Church picnic site
detail: 'In late September and early October, a section of Stream Trail will be shutdown at Old Church Picnic site.' A SEPARATE ROW FROM THE REPAIRS ABOVE because it is a different section and a different window, and merging them would hide that the first has a start date and this one has none. NO DATES ARE STORED AND THE REASON IS THE SCHEMA'S RULE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: 'late September and early October' is not a date, and writing 2026-09-20 or 2026-10-07 would be inventing precision EBRPD did not publish -- the same error as a guessed coordinate or a guessed access mode. starts and ends are left empty and the wording is carried verbatim, so a reader planning a late-September visit sees the words the agency actually used. Filed open-ended, which OVERSTATES it -- this one plainly does end -- and that is the conservative direction for a closure. Re-read the park page before a trip in that window.

summary: BOIL WATER ADVISORY on the drinking water system serving Piedmont Stables.
detail: 'NOTICE TO VISITORS OF PIEDMONT STABLES: The drinking water system serving Piedmont Stables is currently under a Boil Water Advisory.' EBRPD links a Piedmont Stables Water System Boil Water Notice PDF, which has NOT been read here, so the reason, the date it began and what was detected are all unknown. Dated 'Updated September 16, 2026'. THE FIRST DANGER-RATED ADVISORY IN THIS TABLE, and the first water-quality row that is not about algae in a swim beach. Every other water fact this project holds is availability -- is the spigot running -- and this is the other question: it is running and you must not drink it untreated. IT IS FILED AS AN ADVISORY AND NOT AS A WATER SOURCE, which is a schema limit worth naming. water_sources.location must resolve to a trailhead or a campground name, and Piedmont Stables is a staging area and an equestrian facility, so no row can be created for it and no water_source_log entry can record the boil notice against it. The consequence is that this fact reaches a reader through the park it is in rather than through the water table, which works here because Reinhardt Redwood has a campground to hang the park on. DISTANCE FROM THE CAMP IS NOT KNOWN: Piedmont Stables is on Redwood Road near MacDonald Gate, and Girls' Camp is up by Skyline Gate on the far side of the ridge, so this probably does not reach a camper. Probably is not a reason to drop it from a park-scoped table.
